corrected_proposal.title: Trump Names Michael Ellis CIA Deputy Director
corrected_proposal.description_short: An internal, unverified draft isolating the supplied account of Ellis's appointment as CIA deputy director.
corrected_proposal.description_medium: An internal, unverified draft about the supplied packet's account that Donald Trump named Michael Ellis CIA deputy director on February 3, 2025. The packet describes Ellis as a lawyer and former aide to Representative Devin Nunes and says the role does not require Senate confirmation. CIA's accessible announcement confirms Ellis was sworn in as deputy director and lists earlier national-security posts. The selection date, political characterization and confirmation detail remain unverified here.
corrected_proposal.description_long: Michael Ellis was sworn in as Deputy Director of the Central Intelligence Agency, according to the CIA’s announcement. The CIA identifies his earlier service as general counsel of the National Security Agency, senior director for intelligence programs at the National Security Council, general counsel of the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence, and an intelligence officer in the U.S. Navy Reserve. The supplied packet also describes Ellis as a lawyer and former aide to Representative Devin Nunes. The CIA announcement supports the swearing-in and these prior posts; it does not establish the supplied February 3 selection date or characterize Ellis as a political ally. The supplied account says Donald Trump named him on February 3, 2025, but that detail remains unverified here. This record covers the appointment only. It does not combine separate workforce changes or infer loyalty, experience, policy decisions, or misconduct from Ellis’s prior roles.

Deputy Director Ellis previously held a variety of senior national security positions, including General Counsel of the National Security Agency, Senior Director for Intelligence Programs at the National Security Council, and General Counsel of the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence. He also served as an intelligence officer in the US Navy Reserve.
